text.en: Raju's class planted trees and saved water. "Small steps manage the environment," said his teacher.

Conservation is the careful use of natural resources. Forests are important for oxygen, rain, soil protection and wildlife, but deforestation, the clearing of forests, harms them, so forests must be conserved. Wildlife is declining due to habitat loss, and organisations and laws aim to protect species.
Soil erosion is the removal of top soil by wind and water, and it can be managed by planting trees and terracing. Resources are renewable like sunlight and wind, or non-renewable like coal and petroleum, which are fossil fuels that must be conserved.
Solar energy and biogas are alternative energy sources. Shale gas is an unconventional fossil fuel, so it is not renewable. Energy options should be compared by resource use, emissions and local impacts.
Conservation is the careful use of natural resources.
Forests are important for oxygen, rain, soil protection and wildlife, but deforestation, the clearing of forests, harms them, so forests must be conserved.
Wildlife is declining due to habitat loss, and organisations and laws aim to protect species.
Soil erosion is the removal of top soil by wind and water, and it can be managed by planting trees and terracing.
Resources are renewable like sunlight and wind, or non-renewable like coal and petroleum, which are fossil fuels that must be conserved.
Solar energy and biogas are alternatives to conventional fossil fuels. Shale gas is also discussed in the chapter, but it is a non-renewable fossil fuel.
Using a resource carefully leaves more available in the future. Conservation also protects the living systems on which people depend.
Trees store carbon, branches shelter animals, and roots help hold soil. Replacing a forest with a bare slope removes several benefits together.

board.text: Forests offer different benefits at once

text.en: Leaves slow the impact of rain. Roots and litter help water enter the soil. Bare ground often loses more water as fast runoff.

board.text: Forest cover changes how water moves

text.en: A species may lose places to feed or breed even if patches of trees remain. Isolated patches can make movement between populations harder.

board.text: Deforestation can break a habitat into pieces

text.en: New trees need time, suitable soil and protection. Conserving existing habitat and restoring native vegetation can work together.

board.text: Planting is only one part of restoration

text.en: Protecting wildlife often means protecting the place it lives. A species can decline when nesting spaces or food sources disappear.

board.text: A habitat supplies food, water and shelter

text.en: National parks and wildlife sanctuaries help protect species and their habitats. Monitoring can show whether protection is working.
A corridor can connect otherwise separated habitat patches. Animals may use it to find water, mates or shelter.
Compare repeated wildlife counts using a similar method and time of year. A single count can change because animals move or are hard to see.
The upper soil often contains much of the organic matter and supports roots. Losing it can make land less productive.
On a bare slope, running water can pick up loose particles. The soil can settle farther downhill or cloud streams.
Strong wind can lift soil from unprotected ground. Rows of vegetation can slow the wind near the surface.

board.text: Wind can carry dry, exposed soil

text.en: Rows that follow level lines across a slope can slow downhill water flow. Less fast runoff can mean less soil is carried away.

board.text: Contour farming changes the route of runoff

text.en: Steps on a hillside break a long slope into shorter sections. Well-managed terraces can reduce the speed and amount of runoff.
Grass and leaf litter reduce the direct impact of rain and help retain sediment. Roots also help hold particles in place.
Sunlight and wind keep arriving on human timescales. Coal forms much more slowly than we use it.
Coal, oil and natural gas store energy from ancient organisms. Using them depletes deposits that do not quickly return.

board.text: Fossil fuels come from ancient organic material

text.en: A more efficient lamp can provide similar light while using less electricity. Turning unused devices off avoids wasting more.
Solar output varies with cloud, time of day and location. Storage or a mix of sources can help meet demand when output falls.

board.text: Solar panels convert sunlight into electricity

text.en: Microorganisms can produce methane-rich gas from organic material in managed systems. This can recover energy from some kinds of waste.

board.text: Biogas uses breakdown of organic matter

text.en: The word unconventional describes where the gas is found or how it is obtained. It does not mean the resource replenishes quickly.

board.text: Shale gas remains a fossil fuel

text.en: Consider how long the resource lasts, how much pollution it causes, how reliably it meets demand and how it affects local places.

board.text: Compare energy options on more than one measure

text.en: Using daylight or improving efficiency can reduce energy demand. Renewable sources can then supply part of the electricity still needed.
Use habitat protection when species lose shelter. Use soil cover on bare slopes. Use conservation and efficiency when a non-renewable resource is being depleted.

board.text: Match the response to the problem

text.en: Renewable sources do not run out.
Sunlight gives solar energy.
Biogas is also renewable.

problem.en: Two plots receive the same rainfall, but one is bare and one is covered with grass. Which is likely to lose more soil?

text.en: The bare soil is struck directly by rain and runoff can move loose particles.

why.en: Cover slows water near the surface.

text.en: The bare plot is likely to lose more soil, all else being equal.

why.en: Stems and roots help protect the covered plot.

problem.en: Why can a small forest corridor matter between two protected patches?

text.en: Animals may need to move between patches to reach food or mates.

why.en: A road or another barrier can isolate groups.

text.en: A suitable corridor helps connect those habitats.

why.en: Conservation can protect links as well as individual areas.

problem.en: Is shale gas renewable because it is called unconventional?

text.en: No. Its gas comes from a fossil source.

why.en: Unconventional describes the deposit or how it is accessed.

text.en: It is not replaced quickly enough to match its use.

why.en: Renewability depends on the rate of replenishment.

prompt.en: A friend says Coal is a renewable resource. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: Coal takes millions of years to form.

points.en: Solar energy is renewable. Biogas can use replenished organic waste, while shale gas is non-renewable.
